title: Integral scalar-constant constructible sheaves form a weak Serre subcategory
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a finite subextension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Give $\mathcal O_E$ its valuation topology, form the condensed ring $\underline{\mathcal O_E}(S)=C(S,\mathcal O_E)$ on profinite sets [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], and put $R_X=p_X^*\underline{\mathcal O_E}$ on the small pro-étale site of $X$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. In the category $\operatorname{Mod}(R_X)$ of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], call $F$ constructible if it admits a finite locally closed stratification [def-constructible-stratification] on each stratum $T$ of which it is pro-étale locally $R_T\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}P$ with $P$ a finitely presented scalar $\mathcal O_E$-module [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Here finitely presented means that $P$ is the cokernel of a scalar matrix $\mathcal O_E^m\to\mathcal O_E^n$ for finite nonnegative integers $m,n$. The tensor means extension of the constant module sheaf along the constant-section map. Kernels and cokernels, computed in $\operatorname{Mod}(R_X)$, of morphisms between such constructible sheaves are constructible. For any short exact sequence $0\to F'\to F\to F''\to0$ of $R_X$-module sheaves with $F'$ and $F''$ constructible, $F$ is constructible. No finite-type, separatedness, dimension or invertibility hypothesis on $X$ is imposed.

source.place: Definition 6.8.10 and Proposition 6.8.11(1), printed pp. 60–61; scalar-constant integral local models on a topologically Noetherian scheme

proof.text: Write $A=\mathcal O_E$ and choose a uniformizer $\pi$. The affine Noetherian-ring cover in [pqf-def-locnoeth] has a finite subcover by quasi-compactness [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Thus $X$ satisfies precisely the finite-affine-cover meaning of Noetherian used by the adic comparison below. By [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit](3), the actual coefficient ring $R_X=p_X^*\underline A$ is canonically isomorphic to $B_X=\varprojlim_n(A/\pi^n)_X$. The constant scalar $a\in A$ goes to the compatible constant residues $(a\bmod\pi^n)_n$, so the scalar-section maps in the local models agree under this identification. For a stratum immersion $i:T\hookrightarrow X$, [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-immersion-limit-preservation] gives $i^{-1}B_X=\varprojlim_n(A/\pi^n)_T=B_T$, while [sk-def-sfb-constructible] identifies the restricted condensed coefficients with $R_T$. The restricted coefficient isomorphism is the one for $T$: their composites with every finite quotient projection are the same constant-residue maps, so uniqueness of maps to the limit identifies them. On every trivializing cover of $T$, it therefore sends a presentation by a scalar matrix to the presentation by that identical scalar matrix over $B_T$. Thus the two coefficient conventions define precisely the same constructible modules. Transport a module by retaining its abelian sheaf and letting $b\in B_X$ act through the inverse ring isomorphism. This transport and its inverse retain the underlying maps and exact sequences; hence the kernels and cokernels in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] are carried to the corresponding ambient kernels and cokernels. We may work over $B_X$ throughout.

source.place: Definition 6.8.10 and Lemma 6.8.2(1); coefficient identification with Definition 6.5.1

proof.text: Verify the coefficient hypotheses needed for [lem-sfb-adic-stratified-perfect]. By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr](1),(2),(4), $A$ is local with maximal ideal $(\pi)$ and is a PID, hence Noetherian: each ideal has one generator. Put $r=|\pi|_E$, with $0<r<1$. For a compatible family in $\varprojlim_n A/\pi^n$, choose lifts $x_n\in A$. If $m\geq n$, then $x_m-x_n\in\pi^n A$, so $|x_m-x_n|_E\leq r^n$. Completeness [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-complete] gives a limit $x\in E$. The nonarchimedean inequality [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-absolute-value] gives $|x|_E\leq1$ and $|x-x_n|_E\leq r^n$. By the DVR factorization in [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr](5), the latter inequality is equivalent to $x-x_n\in\pi^nA$. Thus $x\in A$ realizes the family. An element of $\bigcap_n\pi^n A$ has norm at most every $r^n$ and is zero. Therefore $A\simeq\varprojlim_n A/\pi^n$, and $(A,I)=(\mathcal O_E,(\pi))$ satisfies all ring hypotheses of that theorem. This argument concerns the coefficient ring alone.

source.place: Definition 6.5.1, specialized to the finite extension coefficients of Definition 6.8.10

proof.text: Use the ordinary unbounded derived category $D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_X))$ and its degree-zero complexes, cohomology and cone triangles [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $\mathcal T$ be the full subcategory specified by condition (2) of [lem-sfb-integral-cohomological-adic-criterion]: derived $(\pi)$-completeness and a bounded constructible étale residue complex of finite Tor amplitude. Its hypotheses are exactly the Noetherian $X$, finite $E$, completed coefficient $B_X$ and scalar finite-presentation convention established above. In particular its constructibility uses $B_T\otimes_A P$, with $P$ finitely presented over the scalar ring $A$, exactly as in this item. By that criterion, $K\in\mathcal T$ if and only if $K$ is bounded and all its cohomology sheaves are constructible. For $(A,I)$ from step 2, this is condition (a) of [lem-sfb-adic-stratified-perfect]. The last paragraph of that theorem therefore makes $\mathcal T$ closed under distinguished triangles with any two vertices in $\mathcal T$. The zero module is constructible using the scalar model $P=0$; for a module $F$ in degree zero, $H^0(F[0])=F$ and all other cohomology vanishes by the cohomology formula in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Hence $F[0]\in\mathcal T$ exactly when $F$ is constructible. No completeness condition has been imposed on arbitrary ambient modules.

source.place: Definition 6.5.1 and its triangulatedness observation; Proposition 6.6.11; Proposition 6.8.11(3), scalar-model characterization

proof.text: Let $f:F\to G$ be a morphism of constructible $B_X$-modules. Then $F[0]$ and $G[0]$ belong to $\mathcal T$ by step 3. The cone triangle of their degree-zero complex map [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] has third vertex represented by $[F\xrightarrow f G]$ in degrees $-1,0$. The two-vertex closure in [lem-sfb-adic-stratified-perfect] puts this cone in $\mathcal T$. The reverse implication of [lem-sfb-integral-cohomological-adic-criterion] makes its cohomology sheaves constructible. Compute them in the abelian module category: at degree $-1$ there is no incoming differential, so $H^{-1}=\ker f$; at degree $0$ the outgoing differential is zero, so $H^0=G/\operatorname{im}f=\operatorname{coker}f$. All other cohomology is zero. Thus these actual ambient kernel and cokernel sheaves, with their given module structures, are constructible. Step 1 returns this assertion to $\operatorname{Mod}(R_X)$.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.11(1), kernel and cokernel clauses; expanded through the scalar-model characterization of (3) and the cone construction

proof.text: Let $0\to F'\to F\to F''\to0$ be the given ambient short exact sequence. Place it in degree zero, obtaining a degreewise short exact sequence of complexes (all other terms are zero). By [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] it gives a distinguished triangle $F'[0]\to F[0]\to F''[0]\to F'[1]$. The constructible ends are in $\mathcal T$ by step 3, so the two-vertex closure in [lem-sfb-adic-stratified-perfect] puts $F[0]$ in $\mathcal T$. By [lem-sfb-integral-cohomological-adic-criterion], its sole cohomology sheaf $F$ is constructible. Transporting back as in step 1 proves extension closure over $R_X$. Every theorem used above allows this arbitrary Noetherian $X$; no step introduces finite type, separatedness, a dimension bound, or invertibility of $\ell$ on $X$.
